the development of molecular materials with novel magnetic properties based on the molecular design and synthesis of metal complexes with free radicals.
the synthesis of novel photomagnetic materials based on the exchange coupling between the unpaired electron of a free radical and the unpaired d-electrons of magnetic metal ions.

the nature of the metal ions and the orientation of the free radical substitu- ents are important factors for the magnetic coupling of the magnetic metal ions with the free radical substituent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photomagnetic properties of the metal-containing organic materials can be controlled by molecular design.
the magnetic properties of these photomagnetic materials are controlled by the nature of the coordination sites on the pyridine base and by the magnetic d-orbitals of the magnetic metal ions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular design of photomagnetic materials can be achieved by the judicious choice of the ligands.
